title: Pulverize the QW sword on June 15
primary_topics: Two converging events that make it imperative for the Supreme Court to pulverize the self-inflicted QW sword and restore impeachment as the exclusive removal mode
House Committee on Justice's 44-0 dismissal of the impeachment complaint against Justice Marvic M. V. F. Leonen (May 27), and its procedural significance
Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos's request for optional retirement (effective June 30, 2021) and the pending certiorari petition basically alleging the same QW grounds
Argument that the Court should waive procedural errors, treat the new pleading as an MR, and decide on the merits invoking the 'transcendental importance' doctrine
Position that pulverizing the QW doctrine would not affect Sereno (not a party in the pending petition) -- her four options laid out
sub_topics: Leonen impeachment grounds: alleged 'lack of integrity' for failure to file SALN at UP for 15 years prior to ascension, and alleged failure to decide cases within 24 months

Procedural-anomaly observation: the House Committee did not return the impeachment complaint for correction of insufficiency in form (per House Rules) -- instead 'dismissed' it with amazing alacrity on May 27, preventing refiling; neither did it determine sufficiency in substance
Constitutional consequence: J Leonen enjoys immunity from impeachment proceedings within one year (Art. XI, Sec. 3-5)
House override mechanism: Sec. 3-3 allows a one-third House override of the Committee's action

Override unlikely because of: (1) the 44-0 unanimity (including Majority Leader Martin Romualdez, a relative of endorser Rep. Angelo Marcos Barba); (2) Speaker Lord Allan Velasco's open backing; (3) unanimous justices' support, as J Leonen himself acknowledged after the 44-0 vote

Delos Santos optional-retirement context: April 18 column noted his pained letter to his staff agonizing over his decision to 'hang (his) judicial robe early' without precise reason; current grounds are 'his current state of health'; retirement effective June 30, 2021 (a year before his 70th birthday June 12, 2022)
Earlier QW petition vs Delos Santos dismissed Feb 18 on procedural errors ('wrong remedy... failure to pay docket fees... etc.')
New certiorari petition basically alleging the same grounds -- on the en banc agenda when the Court resumes June 15
Author's position: treat the new pleading as an MR; waive procedural errors per the 'paralysis of procedural niceties' / 'transcendental importance' exception
Parallel: the Court unanimously supported J Leonen vs impeachment; with 'equal gallantry' it should also unanimously smash the QW sword

Constitutional removal process: (1) one-third House vote for articles; (2) Senate trial; (3) two-thirds Senate concurrence (at least 16 of 24 senators); (4) Constitution makes no mention of QW; (5) no mention of lack of SALN as a removal ground
Republic v. Sereno: simple-majority 8-of-14 vote (CJ inhibited) for SALN failure prior to incumbency, without Senate-style trial

Sereno's four options post-pulverization: ask for reinstatement as CJ or as AJ; apply for reappointment via the usual constitutional process; receive retirement benefits similar to those granted to CJ Renato C. Corona; or do nothing

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban argues that two converging events make it imperative for the Supreme Court to 'pulverize' the self-inflicted sword of quo warranto (QW) and restore the constitutional shroud of judicial independence -- by limiting justice removal to impeachment -- at its en banc resumption on June 15. The first is the May 27 dismissal, 44-0, by the House Committee on Justice of the impeachment complaint against Justice Marvic M. V. F. Leonen for alleged 'lack of integrity' (failure to file SALN at UP for 15 years prior to his ascension) and failure to decide cases within 24 months -- a dismissal accomplished, he observes, with 'amazing alacrity' that bypassed the House Rules' return-for-insufficiency-in-form procedure, foreclosed refiling, and skipped sufficiency-in-substance determination, while conferring the one-year impeachment immunity under Art. XI Sec. 3-5. The override mechanism in Sec. 3-3 (one-third House vote) is unlikely given (1) the 44-0 unanimity (including Majority Leader Martin Romualdez, a relative of endorser Rep. Angelo Marcos Barba), (2) Speaker Lord Allan Velasco's open backing, and (3) unanimous justices' support, as Leonen himself acknowledged. The second is Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos's early retirement (approved by the Court 'due to his current state of health,' effective June 30, 2021 -- a year before his 70th birthday) and the new certiorari petition basically alleging the same grounds as the dismissed Feb 18 QW petition (which fell on procedural errors -- wrong remedy, failure to pay docket fees, etc.), now on the en banc agenda. Panganiban argues that the Court should waive the procedural errors, treat the new pleading as a motion for reconsideration, and decide on the merits -- invoking the 'transcendental importance' jurisprudence that exempts cases from 'the paralysis of procedural niceties' -- because the Court's independence is of the highest transcendental importance and should be 'frontally faced at this first available opportunity.' He frames the call by paralleling Leonen: 'Gallantly, the Court unanimously supported J Leonen in the impeachment attempt; with equal gallantry, it should also unanimously smash the QW sword to protect not just one member but all incumbent and future members.' He restates the constitutional case -- impeachment requires one-third House vote, Senate trial, and two-thirds Senate concurrence (at least 16 of 24 senators); the Constitution makes no mention, not even a hint, of QW as a removal method, nor of lack of SALNs as a removal ground; yet the Court ousted CJ Sereno via QW for SALN failure prior to incumbency on a simple 8-of-14 majority (CJ inhibited) and without Senate-style trial. He closes by arguing that pulverizing QW would not affect Sereno because she is not a party in the pending petition, but her four post-pulverization options -- reinstatement as CJ or AJ, reappointment via the usual constitutional process, Corona-style retirement benefits, or doing nothing -- remain available.
